Ethereum ( CRYPTO:ETH ) has a market value 37.2 times that of Cardano ( CRYPTO:ADA ), a blockchain network created as a competitor. Ethereum has a market cap of approximately $285.2 billion, while Cardano’s is around $7.7 billion, with ETH priced at nearly $2,335 and ADA at about $0.20. This significant disparity highlights the current state of the Ethereum vs. Cardano rivalry. Current investor sentiment isn’t helping Cardano. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index, which measures market sentiment on a scale of 0 to 100, is at 40, indicating “Fear.” Additionally, the total value of the cryptocurrency market has decreased by 0.3% in the past 24 hours. While Cardano has shown stronger growth in certain periods, increasing by 34.0% over the last 90 days compared to Ethereum’s 24.6% increase, it has faced recent challenges. ADA has fall en 17.3% in just two weeks and trades 93.4% below its September 1, 2021 peak of $3.09 . This raises the question: Is Cardano fundamentally undervalued, or is the market correctly assessing its worth? Market capitalization, calculated by multiplying the number of coins in circulation by their current price, places Ethereum as the second-largest cryptocurrency , with Cardano at 18th. Traders often interpret a large market cap gap as a sign of investor sentiment, with a wider gap suggesting buyers value Ethereum more for its anticipated future use. In theory, a smaller market cap like Cardano’s could signal growth potential because it requires less new investment to raise its price. However, this hasn’t held true recently. Over the past year, ETH fell 40.4%, while ADA fell even more, 68.1%. Over five years, ETH lost 43.2%, while ADA fell 90.3%. Each time the market turned down, Cardano lost more ground, suggesting investors view ADA as riskier. Market cap calculations have their limitations. They value assets based on the most recent trade price, so trading activity in a thin market can drive price volatility. Trading volume better reflects market depth, with Ethereum seeing about $8.4 billion in trades in the last 24 hours compared to just $213.7 million for Cardano. However, a significant portion of trading volume comes from automated programs known as market-making bots, which facilitate buying and selling throughout the day. Despite this, Ethereum’s deeper market allows larger investors to trade without significantly impacting the price, attracting institutional investment. Another factor to consider is supply dilution—this occurs when new coins enter circulation. About 37.6 billion ADA are in circulation out of a maximum of 45 billion, giving a fully diluted valuation (the value if all coins were trading) of about $9.2 billion. In contrast, Ethereum’s fully diluted value matches its market cap, making Cardano more susceptible to future supply increases. Ethereum also benefits from regulatory approval. As of October 22, U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs , which are funds that hold ETH and trade similarly to stocks, collectively managed $14.6 billion in assets, with a significant $12.7 billion in net inflows. Cardano, on the other hand, lacks a similar financial instrument. Grayscale withdrew its application for a Cardano Trust ETF on August 7, and that was the only dedicated U.S. spot ADA product in progress. Ethereum’s lead is also bolstered by network effects, meaning that as more users join the Ethereum network, its usefulness increases. Most stablecoins (tokens pegged to the U.S. dollar), DeFi applications (financial services operating on code), and tokenized funds are built on Ethereum. New projects tend to gravitate toward the more established network, further widening the usage gap. On both networks, most transactions occur on exchanges and don’t reach the blockchain, so a quieter Cardano network may suggest buyers are accumulating ADA or hesitating to buy—on-chain data can’t clarify the situation. The market gap could narrow on Ethereum’s side. On October 22, Ethereum ETFs reported a net outflow of $110.5 million, with the largest single-day outflow recently reaching $201.9 million on October 6. Cumulative inflows have decreased from $14.0 billion to $12.7 billion since September 28. On the Cardano side, the network supported the SEC’s proposed “Regulation Crypto Assets” in a comment letter, as reported on October 21. Although this shows support, it has little immediate effect. The regulation could help ADA’s price if it simplifies launching new U.S. products—assuming a sponsor eventually steps forward to file one. On October 21, Cardano’s founder, Charles Hoskinson, welcomed TRON ( CRYPTO:TRX ) to Midnight ( CRYPTO:NIGHT ), Cardano’s privacy-focused partner chain, with the integration expected in December. However, payments from that collaboration would benefit Midnight first and reach ADA only indirectly. Yet, Hoskinson has faced scrutiny over a new programming language he says he is developing for Cardano, which lacks a technical specification. This has sparked skepticism in the community, making it clear that Cardano faces both challenges and opportunities ahead. We don’t expect the significant 37.2x gap between Ethereum (ETH) and Cardano (ADA) to close much. The Fear reading of 40 suggests investors are pricing Cardano appropriately, since ADA hasn’t attracted significant new funds. For those holding ADA , the challenge is that the coin has dropped 68.1% over the past year and could continue to lag behind ETH. For Cardano to close this gap, it would likely need a strong push. This could come from a new spot ADA exchange-traded fund (ETF) that attracts investment, or from stablecoin projects or tokenized funds choosing to use its blockchain. Unfortunately, Cardano has yet to see any of these developments. A key price point to watch is ADA rising above $0.26, which was its value on September 25. Ethereum ( CRYPTO:ETH ) has a market value 37.2 times that of Cardano ( CRYPTO:ADA ), a blockchain network created as a competitor. Ethereum has a market cap of approximately $285.2 billion, while Cardano’s is around $7.7 billion, with ETH priced at nearly $2,335 and ADA at about $0.20. This significant disparity highlights the current state of the Ethereum vs. Cardano rivalry.

Current investor sentiment isn’t helping Cardano. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index, which measures market sentiment on a scale of 0 to 100, is at 40, indicating “Fear.” Additionally, the total value of the cryptocurrency market has decreased by 0.3% in the past 24 hours.

While Cardano has shown stronger growth in certain periods, increasing by 34.0% over the last 90 days compared to Ethereum’s 24.6% increase, it has faced recent challenges. ADA has fall en 17.3% in just two weeks and trades 93.4% below its September 1, 2021 peak of $3.09 . This raises the question: Is Cardano fundamentally undervalued, or is the market correctly assessing its worth?

Market capitalization, calculated by multiplying the number of coins in circulation by their current price, places Ethereum as the second-largest cryptocurrency , with Cardano at 18th. Traders often interpret a large market cap gap as a sign of investor sentiment, with a wider gap suggesting buyers value Ethereum more for its anticipated future use.
In theory, a smaller market cap like Cardano’s could signal growth potential because it requires less new investment to raise its price. However, this hasn’t held true recently.

Over the past year, ETH fell 40.4%, while ADA fell even more, 68.1%. Over five years, ETH lost 43.2%, while ADA fell 90.3%. Each time the market turned down, Cardano lost more ground, suggesting investors view ADA as riskier.

Market cap calculations have their limitations. They value assets based on the most recent trade price, so trading activity in a thin market can drive price volatility. Trading volume better reflects market depth, with Ethereum seeing about $8.4 billion in trades in the last 24 hours compared to just $213.7 million for Cardano.

However, a significant portion of trading volume comes from automated programs known as market-making bots, which facilitate buying and selling throughout the day. Despite this, Ethereum’s deeper market allows larger investors to trade without significantly impacting the price, attracting institutional investment.

Another factor to consider is supply dilution—this occurs when new coins enter circulation. About 37.6 billion ADA are in circulation out of a maximum of 45 billion, giving a fully diluted valuation (the value if all coins were trading) of about $9.2 billion. In contrast, Ethereum’s fully diluted value matches its market cap, making Cardano more susceptible to future supply increases.

Ethereum also benefits from regulatory approval. As of October 22, U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs , which are funds that hold ETH and trade similarly to stocks, collectively managed $14.6 billion in assets, with a significant $12.7 billion in net inflows. Cardano, on the other hand, lacks a similar financial instrument. Grayscale withdrew its application for a Cardano Trust ETF on August 7, and that was the only dedicated U.S. spot ADA product in progress.

Ethereum’s lead is also bolstered by network effects, meaning that as more users join the Ethereum network, its usefulness increases. Most stablecoins (tokens pegged to the U.S. dollar), DeFi applications (financial services operating on code), and tokenized funds are built on Ethereum. New projects tend to gravitate toward the more established network, further widening the usage gap.

On both networks, most transactions occur on exchanges and don’t reach the blockchain, so a quieter Cardano network may suggest buyers are accumulating ADA or hesitating to buy—on-chain data can’t clarify the situation.

The market gap could narrow on Ethereum’s side. On October 22, Ethereum ETFs reported a net outflow of $110.5 million, with the largest single-day outflow recently reaching $201.9 million on October 6. Cumulative inflows have decreased from $14.0 billion to $12.7 billion since September 28.

On the Cardano side, the network supported the SEC’s proposed “Regulation Crypto Assets” in a comment letter, as reported on October 21. Although this shows support, it has little immediate effect. The regulation could help ADA’s price if it simplifies launching new U.S. products—assuming a sponsor eventually steps forward to file one.

On October 21, Cardano’s founder, Charles Hoskinson, welcomed TRON ( CRYPTO:TRX ) to Midnight ( CRYPTO:NIGHT ), Cardano’s privacy-focused partner chain, with the integration expected in December. However, payments from that collaboration would benefit Midnight first and reach ADA only indirectly.

Yet, Hoskinson has faced scrutiny over a new programming language he says he is developing for Cardano, which lacks a technical specification. This has sparked skepticism in the community, making it clear that Cardano faces both challenges and opportunities ahead.

We don’t expect the significant 37.2x gap between Ethereum (ETH) and Cardano (ADA) to close much. The Fear reading of 40 suggests investors are pricing Cardano appropriately, since ADA hasn’t attracted significant new funds. For those holding ADA , the challenge is that the coin has dropped 68.1% over the past year and could continue to lag behind ETH.

For Cardano to close this gap, it would likely need a strong push. This could come from a new spot ADA exchange-traded fund (ETF) that attracts investment, or from stablecoin projects or tokenized funds choosing to use its blockchain. Unfortunately, Cardano has yet to see any of these developments.

A key price point to watch is ADA rising above $0.26, which was its value on September 25. If ADA remains around $0.20 while Ethereum’s ETF outflows stabilize, the gap could either hold steady or widen further.

passages: Cardano was built to challenge Ethereum, yet it keeps losing ground faster whenever the market turns. Understanding what separates these two blockchains reveals why closing that gap may require much more than just lower prices and ambitious promises.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Ethereum ( CRYPTO:ETH ) has a market value 37.2 times that of Cardano ( CRYPTO:ADA ), a blockchain network created as a competitor. Ethereum has a market cap of approximately $285.2 billion, while Cardano’s is around $7.7 billion, with ETH priced at nearly $2,335 and ADA at about $0.20. This significant disparity highlights the current state of the Ethereum vs. Cardano rivalry.

Current investor sentiment isn’t helping Cardano. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index, which measures market sentiment on a scale of 0 to 100, is at 40, indicating “Fear.” Additionally, the total value of the cryptocurrency market has decreased by 0.3% in the past 24 hours.

While Cardano has shown stronger growth in certain periods, increasing by 34.0% over the last 90 days compared to Ethereum’s 24.6% increase, it has faced recent challenges. ADA has fall en 17.3% in just two weeks and trades 93.4% below its September 1, 2021 peak of $3.09 . This raises the question: Is Cardano fundamentally undervalued, or is the market correctly assessing its worth?

Market capitalization, calculated by multiplying the number of coins in circulation by their current price, places Ethereum as the second-largest cryptocurrency , with Cardano at 18th. Traders often interpret a large market cap gap as a sign of investor sentiment, with a wider gap suggesting buyers value Ethereum more for its anticipated future use.
In theory, a smaller market cap like Cardano’s could signal growth potential because it requires less new investment to raise its price. However, this hasn’t held true recently.

Over the past year, ETH fell 40.4%, while ADA fell even more, 68.1%. Over five years, ETH lost 43.2%, while ADA fell 90.3%. Each time the market turned down, Cardano lost more ground, suggesting investors view ADA as riskier.

Market cap calculations have their limitations. They value assets based on the most recent trade price, so trading activity in a thin market can drive price volatility. Trading volume better reflects market depth, with Ethereum seeing about $8.4 billion in trades in the last 24 hours compared to just $213.7 million for Cardano.

However, a significant portion of trading volume comes from automated programs known as market-making bots, which facilitate buying and selling throughout the day. Despite this, Ethereum’s deeper market allows larger investors to trade without significantly impacting the price, attracting institutional investment.

Another factor to consider is supply dilution—this occurs when new coins enter circulation. About 37.6 billion ADA are in circulation out of a maximum of 45 billion, giving a fully diluted valuation (the value if all coins were trading) of about $9.2 billion. In contrast, Ethereum’s fully diluted value matches its market cap, making Cardano more susceptible to future supply increases.

Ethereum also benefits from regulatory approval. As of October 22, U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs , which are funds that hold ETH and trade similarly to stocks, collectively managed $14.6 billion in assets, with a significant $12.7 billion in net inflows. Cardano, on the other hand, lacks a similar financial instrument. Grayscale withdrew its application for a Cardano Trust ETF on August 7, and that was the only dedicated U.S. spot ADA product in progress.

Ethereum’s lead is also bolstered by network effects, meaning that as more users join the Ethereum network, its usefulness increases. Most stablecoins (tokens pegged to the U.S. dollar), DeFi applications (financial services operating on code), and tokenized funds are built on Ethereum. New projects tend to gravitate toward the more established network, further widening the usage gap.

On both networks, most transactions occur on exchanges and don’t reach the blockchain, so a quieter Cardano network may suggest buyers are accumulating ADA or hesitating to buy—on-chain data can’t clarify the situation.

The market gap could narrow on Ethereum’s side. On October 22, Ethereum ETFs reported a net outflow of $110.5 million, with the largest single-day outflow recently reaching $201.9 million on October 6. Cumulative inflows have decreased from $14.0 billion to $12.7 billion since September 28.

On the Cardano side, the network supported the SEC’s proposed “Regulation Crypto Assets” in a comment letter, as reported on October 21. Although this shows support, it has little immediate effect. The regulation could help ADA’s price if it simplifies launching new U.S. products—assuming a sponsor eventually steps forward to file one.

On October 21, Cardano’s founder, Charles Hoskinson, welcomed TRON ( CRYPTO:TRX ) to Midnight ( CRYPTO:NIGHT ), Cardano’s privacy-focused partner chain, with the integration expected in December. However, payments from that collaboration would benefit Midnight first and reach ADA only indirectly.

Yet, Hoskinson has faced scrutiny over a new programming language he says he is developing for Cardano, which lacks a technical specification. This has sparked skepticism in the community, making it clear that Cardano faces both challenges and opportunities ahead.

We don’t expect the significant 37.2x gap between Ethereum (ETH) and Cardano (ADA) to close much. The Fear reading of 40 suggests investors are pricing Cardano appropriately, since ADA hasn’t attracted significant new funds. For those holding ADA , the challenge is that the coin has dropped 68.1% over the past year and could continue to lag behind ETH.

For Cardano to close this gap, it would likely need a strong push. This could come from a new spot ADA exchange-traded fund (ETF) that attracts investment, or from stablecoin projects or tokenized funds choosing to use its blockchain. Unfortunately, Cardano has yet to see any of these developments.

A key price point to watch is ADA rising above $0.26, which was its value on September 25. If ADA remains around $0.20 while Ethereum’s ETF outflows stabilize, the gap could either hold steady or widen further.

Zcash ( CRYPTO: ZEC ) rose 7.5% in the week ending October 25, 2026, while Monero (CRYPTO: XMR ) gained 3.8%. In contrast, Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ) fell 2%. Zcash is currently priced at $1,208, and Monero at $606. Notably, Monero has climbed 13.6% over the last 14 days, whereas Bitcoin has fallen by 3.3%.

Privacy coins are cryptocurrencies designed to keep transactions private by hiding the sender, recipient, and transaction amount. Despite their recent gains, Zcash and Monero look weaker over longer periods. Zcash is down 24.1% over the last 30 days and trades 62.2% below its 2016 all-time high. Monero is also facing challenges, trading 24% below its January peak of $797.73.

Bitcoin’s recent struggles stem from external factors. On October 22, Brent crude oil prices soared above $111 a barrel, raising inflation concerns and reducing demand for speculative investments like cryptocurrencies. Asian and U.S. stocks also slipped on doubts about AI spending, and Bitcoin fell to $79,107 on October 24.

Zcash drew attention with its upcoming network upgrade, NU7 , scheduled for around November 5. This upgrade aims to significantly speed up payment confirmations by reducing the block time from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. Additionally, the upgrade will temporarily remove 60% of each block’s fees from circulation until February 2031, which investors generally welcome because it may reduce supply.

Zcash saw a notable 16.5% price increase, rising from $1,129 on October 18 to $1,316 by October 21. While the timing of this spike aligns with the upgrade announcement, it is still difficult to determine its cause conclusively.

Monero’s recent upswing can be partly linked to a regulatory shift. On October 5, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) rescinded a proposal that could have imposed stricter regulations on crypto mixing—the technique used to obscure transaction origins, similar to privacy coins. This change likely boosted market sentiment, helping drive Monero’s 14-day price increase.

Monero is also preparing for a major upgrade, FCMP++, that aims to significantly enhance privacy features. Although still in testing, it could potentially obscure transaction sources among over 150 million candidates, a sizable jump from the 16 candidates under the current design.

A short squeeze could also have aided Monero’s rise. A short squeeze occurs when traders holding short positions are forced to buy an asset back at higher prices to cover their positions. However, data on liquidation totals for the past week has not been released, so this remains speculative.

Zcash’s recent gains occurred within a continuing downtrend, characterized by a series of lower highs and lower lows. After hitting an intraday high of $1,693 on September 26, ZEC fell to $1,048 by October 18 before rebounding to $1,373 on October 21. However, this recovery was short-lived, as ZEC closed at $1,218 on October 22, $1,182 on October 23, and $1,207 on October 24.

Moreover, trading volume decreased, with daily volume exceeding 100,000 ZEC during a brief surge from October 20 to 22, then falling. When a rally loses momentum in trading volume, it often suggests new buyers aren’t stepping in to replace those who initially drove the price up, indicating the price bounce may not reflect a strong new trend.

Bitcoin’s market behavior has recently mirrored that of macroeconomic factors. Oil prices and stock market shifts directly affect its performance. Conversely, privacy coins like Monero and Zcash respond to a distinct investor base that prioritizes transaction anonymity. Their markets are less active, leading to larger price swings on smaller inflows and outflows.

In addition, Zcash benefits from recent institutional interest. The Grayscale Zcash ETF ( NYSEARCA: ZCSH ) launched on August 25, allowing U.S. investors to access ZEC through standard brokerage accounts, and Zcash has risen 136.6% year-to-date. This contrasts sharply with Bitcoin, which has fallen 7.7% during the same period.

Zcash ( CRYPTO: ZEC ) rose 7.5% in the week ending October 25, 2026, while Monero (CRYPTO: XMR ) gained 3.8%. In contrast, Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ) fell 2%. Zcash is currently priced at $1,208, and Monero at $606. Notably, Monero has climbed 13.6% over the last 14 days, whereas Bitcoin has fallen by 3.3%.

Privacy coins are cryptocurrencies designed to keep transactions private by hiding the sender, recipient, and transaction amount. Despite their recent gains, Zcash and Monero look weaker over longer periods. Zcash is down 24.1% over the last 30 days and trades 62.2% below its 2016 all-time high. Monero is also facing challenges, trading 24% below its January peak of $797.73.

Bitcoin’s recent struggles stem from external factors. On October 22, Brent crude oil prices soared above $111 a barrel, raising inflation concerns and reducing demand for speculative investments like cryptocurrencies. Asian and U.S. stocks also slipped on doubts about AI spending, and Bitcoin fell to $79,107 on October 24.

Zcash drew attention with its upcoming network upgrade, NU7 , scheduled for around November 5. This upgrade aims to significantly speed up payment confirmations by reducing the block time from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. Additionally, the upgrade will temporarily remove 60% of each block’s fees from circulation until February 2031, which investors generally welcome because it may reduce supply.

Zcash saw a notable 16.5% price increase, rising from $1,129 on October 18 to $1,316 by October 21. While the timing of this spike aligns with the upgrade announcement, it is still difficult to determine its cause conclusively.

Monero’s recent upswing can be partly linked to a regulatory shift. On October 5, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) rescinded a proposal that could have imposed stricter regulations on crypto mixing—the technique used to obscure transaction origins, similar to privacy coins. This change likely boosted market sentiment, helping drive Monero’s 14-day price increase.

Monero is also preparing for a major upgrade, FCMP++, that aims to significantly enhance privacy features. Although still in testing, it could potentially obscure transaction sources among over 150 million candidates, a sizable jump from the 16 candidates under the current design.

A short squeeze could also have aided Monero’s rise. A short squeeze occurs when traders holding short positions are forced to buy an asset back at higher prices to cover their positions. However, data on liquidation totals for the past week has not been released, so this remains speculative.

Zcash’s recent gains occurred within a continuing downtrend, characterized by a series of lower highs and lower lows. After hitting an intraday high of $1,693 on September 26, ZEC fell to $1,048 by October 18 before rebounding to $1,373 on October 21. However, this recovery was short-lived, as ZEC closed at $1,218 on October 22, $1,182 on October 23, and $1,207 on October 24.

Moreover, trading volume decreased, with daily volume exceeding 100,000 ZEC during a brief surge from October 20 to 22, then falling. When a rally loses momentum in trading volume, it often suggests new buyers aren’t stepping in to replace those who initially drove the price up, indicating the price bounce may not reflect a strong new trend.

Bitcoin’s market behavior has recently mirrored that of macroeconomic factors. Oil prices and stock market shifts directly affect its performance. Conversely, privacy coins like Monero and Zcash respond to a distinct investor base that prioritizes transaction anonymity. Their markets are less active, leading to larger price swings on smaller inflows and outflows.

The Grayscale Zcash ETF ( NYSEARCA: ZCSH ) launched on August 25, allowing U.S. investors to access ZEC through standard brokerage accounts, and Zcash has risen 136.6% year-to-date. This contrasts sharply with Bitcoin, which has fallen 7.7% during the same period.

Monero, however, primarily trades on cryptocurrency exchanges, and regulatory concerns have led several platforms to delist it. This has resulted in a more dedicated but less active investor base, which may explain its more modest 3.8% gain.

sources.title: JPMorgan Has Nearly $900 Million in Tokenized Funds on Ethereum and Solana. Which Chain Benefits More? - Yahoo Finance
passages: JPMorgan deployed nearly $900 million in tokenized funds on Ethereum and Solana, with JLTXX holding $792 million and MONY holding $103 million on Ethereum.
A tokenized fund is an investment fund whose shares exist as tokens on a blockchain, allowing them to trade around the clock.
These tokenized funds bring in modest revenue compared to JPMorgan's core businesses.
Fees from these funds contribute to Asset & Wealth Management, which manages over $5.1 trillion in client assets, while payments revenue, including JPMD, grew 12% in the second quarter.
MONY's $103.1 million is entirely Ethereum-based, JLTXX launched there first, and JPMD integrated into Ethereum before any other chain besides Base.
Because Base is an Ethereum layer-2 network, the $1 million JPMD supply also links back to Ethereum.
ETH has declined 12.5% over the past month, while SOL's value has fallen 16.1%, trends that far outweigh the impact of a few hundred million dollars in funds.
JPMorgan and the respective coins gain different advantages from this move.
While both networks use a portion of their fees for validator rewards, the flow is negligible at these fund sizes.
When explaining its choice of Ethereum, JPMorgan cited its "established depth of on-chain liquidity and tokenized assets," yet Sentora still shows no JPMD supply on Ethereum.
Morgan Asset Management, said clients operate across multiple networks, so their liquidity should reflect that need.
However, he did not provide specific figures to back that demand.

passages: JPMorgan just parked nearly $900 million in tokenized funds across Ethereum and Solana, but the fine print reveals one chain got a much bigger piece of the deal than the headlines suggest.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

JPMorgan Chase ( NYSE: JPM | JPM Price Prediction ) has made headlines by placing nearly $900 million in tokenized funds on both Ethereum ( CRYPTO: ETH ) and Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ). A tokenized fund is an investment fund whose shares exist as tokens on a blockchain, allowing them to trade around the clock.

According to Sentora data, the JPMorgan OnChain Liquidity-Token Money Market Fund (JLTXX) holds about $792 million across both networks, while the My OnChain Net Yield Fund (MONY) holds an estimated $103.1 million on Ethereum alone.

In just one week, JPMorgan took two significant steps. On October 19, 2026, Kinexys, the bank’s blockchain unit, introduced its JPM Coin deposit token (JPMD) to Ethereum. Shortly after, on October 22, J.P. Morgan Asset Management launched MONY and JLTXX on Solana. However, despite these announcements, both cryptocurrencies saw declines: ETH fell to $2,333, down 2.1% for the week, while SOL dropped to $101, down 1.5%.

JLTXX is a U.S.-registered government money market fund that invests cash in short-term government debt and passes interest earnings directly to investors. JPMorgan designed it so that stablecoin issuers can hold reserves in JLTXX tokens under the GENIUS Act, a federal stablecoin law. JPMorgan first launched JLTXX on Ethereum in May.

MONY, by contrast, is a private placement regulated under the SEC’s Rule 506(c), meaning only high-net-worth individuals can invest. JPMorgan rolled this fund out in December 2025. Both funds operate through Morgan Money, JPMorgan’s cash management platform, allowing investors to subscribe and redeem, then receive tokens at a designated blockchain address. Retail traders cannot purchase these tokens on exchanges.

Meanwhile, JPMD is a deposit token representing a dollar held in a JPMorgan bank account, enabling institutional clients to transact at any time. It initially launched on Base, the blockchain connected to Coinbase ( NASDAQ: COIN ), where Sentora reports a $1 million supply, but it is not yet available on Ethereum.

These tokenized funds bring in modest revenue compared to JPMorgan’s core businesses. Fees from these funds contribute to Asset & Wealth Management, which manages over $5.1 trillion in client assets, while payments revenue, including JPMD, grew 12% in the second quarter. Additionally, neither Sentora nor JPMorgan has disclosed how JLTXX’s $792 million is split between Ethereum and Solana, making it hard to say Solana has a significant share.

The announcements did not commit anyone to buy or hold ETH or SOL. When a tokenized fund moves its assets, it incurs small transaction fees known as gas. However, money market fund tokens mainly sit in a few institutional wallets, so they generate far less fee activity than stablecoin transfers or trading.

The Solana announcement notably excluded details about the on-chain cash used to trade the fund tokens. It mentioned Morgan Money as the subscription channel but did not reference any stablecoin or JPMD for Solana. Until JPMorgan identifies an on-chain cash option for Solana, the bank’s own dollars will remain absent from that chain.

When explaining its choice of Ethereum, JPMorgan cited its “established depth of on-chain liquidity and tokenized assets,” yet Sentora still shows no JPMD supply on Ethereum. Paul Przybylski, who leads digital and tokenized assets at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, said clients operate across multiple networks, so their liquidity should reflect that need. However, he did not provide specific figures to back that demand.

JPMorgan’s timing on Solana also could be considered late, as competitors like BlackRock ( NYSE: BLK ) and Franklin Templeton introduced tokenized funds there in 2025. Currently, the market appears to be contracting, with Sentora reporting $14.4 billion in tokenized Treasury and money market products across 119 offerings, a 3.5% decline over the past month.

Ethereum currently leads JPMorgan’s tokenized funds. MONY’s $103.1 million is entirely Ethereum-based, JLTXX launched there first, and JPMD integrated into Ethereum before any other chain besides Base. Because Base is an Ethereum layer-2 network, the $1 million JPMD supply also links back to Ethereum.

JPMorgan and the respective coins gain different advantages from this move. JPMorgan stands to benefit from fee-generating fund assets and a reserve product tailored for stablecoin issuers, while Ethereum and Solana gain enhanced credibility and the potential for increased stablecoin and trading activity stemming from involvement with a prominent bank like JPMorgan. While both networks use a portion of their fees for validator rewards , the flow is negligible at these fund sizes.

For now, Ethereum appears to benefit more from JPMorgan’s tokenized funds, though neither asset has guaranteed buyers. ETH has declined 12.5% over the past month, while SOL’s value has fallen 16.1%, trends that far outweigh the impact of a few hundred million dollars in funds.

Solana could gain ground if JPMorgan names it as a JPMD network, giving the funds an on-chain cash option there, or if a Solana-based stablecoin issuer starts holding its reserves in JLTXX. If JPMD’s Ethereum supply rises above zero before JPMorgan announces anything for Solana, Ethereum’s lead likely holds, but a Solana JPMD launch first could start shifting the advantage to SOL.

JPMorgan Chase ( NYSE: JPM ) has made headlines by placing nearly $900 million in tokenized funds on both Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) and Solana (CRYPTO: SOL). A tokenized fund is an investment fund whose shares exist as tokens on a blockchain, allowing them to trade around the clock.

According to Sentora data, the JPMorgan OnChain Liquidity-Token Money Market Fund (JLTXX) holds about $792 million across both networks, while the My OnChain Net Yield Fund (MONY) holds an estimated $103.1 million on Ethereum alone.

In just one week, JPMorgan took two significant steps. On October 19, 2026, Kinexys, the bank's blockchain unit, introduced its JPM Coin deposit token (JPMD) to Ethereum. Shortly after, on October 22, J.P. Morgan Asset Management launched MONY and JLTXX on Solana. However, despite these announcements, both cryptocurrencies saw declines: ETH fell to $2,333, down 2.1% for the week, while SOL dropped to $101, down 1.5%.

JLTXX is a U.S.-registered government money market fund that invests cash in short-term government debt and passes interest earnings directly to investors. JPMorgan designed it so that stablecoin issuers can hold reserves in JLTXX tokens under the GENIUS Act, a federal stablecoin law. JPMorgan first launched JLTXX on Ethereum in May.

MONY, by contrast, is a private placement regulated under the SEC's Rule 506(c), meaning only high-net-worth individuals can invest. JPMorgan rolled this fund out in December 2025. Both funds operate through Morgan Money, JPMorgan's cash management platform, allowing investors to subscribe and redeem, then receive tokens at a designated blockchain address. Retail traders cannot purchase these tokens on exchanges.

Meanwhile, JPMD is a deposit token representing a dollar held in a JPMorgan bank account, enabling institutional clients to transact at any time. It initially launched on Base, the blockchain connected to Coinbase ( NASDAQ: COIN ), where Sentora reports a $1 million supply, but it is not yet available on Ethereum.

These tokenized funds bring in modest revenue compared to JPMorgan's core businesses. Fees from these funds contribute to Asset & Wealth Management, which manages over $5.1 trillion in client assets, while payments revenue, including JPMD, grew 12% in the second quarter. Additionally, neither Sentora nor JPMorgan has disclosed how JLTXX's $792 million is split between Ethereum and Solana, making it hard to say Solana has a significant share.

The announcements did not commit anyone to buy or hold ETH or SOL. When a tokenized fund moves its assets, it incurs small transaction fees known as gas. However, money market fund tokens mainly sit in a few institutional wallets, so they generate far less fee activity than stablecoin transfers or trading.

The Solana announcement notably excluded details about the on-chain cash used to trade the fund tokens. It mentioned Morgan Money as the subscription channel but did not reference any stablecoin or JPMD for Solana. Until JPMorgan identifies an on-chain cash option for Solana, the bank's own dollars will remain absent from that chain.

When explaining its choice of Ethereum, JPMorgan cited its "established depth of on-chain liquidity and tokenized assets," yet Sentora still shows no JPMD supply on Ethereum. Paul Przybylski, who leads digital and tokenized assets at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, said clients operate across multiple networks, so their liquidity should reflect that need. However, he did not provide specific figures to back that demand.

JPMorgan's timing on Solana also could be considered late, as competitors like BlackRock ( NYSE: BLK ) and Franklin Templeton introduced tokenized funds there in 2025. Currently, the market appears to be contracting, with Sentora reporting $14.4 billion in tokenized Treasury and money market products across 119 offerings, a 3.5% decline over the past month.

Ethereum currently leads JPMorgan's tokenized funds. MONY's $103.1 million is entirely Ethereum-based, JLTXX launched there first, and JPMD integrated into Ethereum before any other chain besides Base. Because Base is an Ethereum layer-2 network, the $1 million JPMD supply also links back to Ethereum.

JPMorgan and the respective coins gain different advantages from this move. JPMorgan stands to benefit from fee-generating fund assets and a reserve product tailored for stablecoin issuers, while Ethereum and Solana gain enhanced credibility and the potential for increased stablecoin and trading activity stemming from involvement with a prominent bank like JPMorgan. While both networks use a portion of their fees for validator rewards, the flow is negligible at these fund sizes.

For now, Ethereum appears to benefit more from JPMorgan's tokenized funds, though neither asset has guaranteed buyers. ETH has declined 12.5% over the past month, while SOL's value has fallen 16.1%, trends that far outweigh the impact of a few hundred million dollars in funds.

Solana could gain ground if JPMorgan names it as a JPMD network, giving the funds an on-chain cash option there, or if a Solana-based stablecoin issuer starts holding its reserves in JLTXX. If JPMD's Ethereum supply rises above zero before JPMorgan announces anything for Solana, Ethereum's lead likely holds, but a Solana JPMD launch first could start shifting the advantage to SOL.

Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ) has once again fallen below $80,000, briefly hitting $79,973 before buyers stepped in and pushed it back up to $80,287. This decline followed a sharper drop the day before, when Bitcoin sank to $79,220 on Binance, marking weekly lows at $79,107, its weakest point in over a month.

While this drop may seem limited, Bitcoin is down 3.3% for October but still up 26.8% over the last 90 days; the $80,000 threshold matters to its largest holders. Bitcoin last traded at or below $77,600 on September 18, so what caused this dip, and how much further could it fall?

External factors largely drove the downturn. Reports on October 24 indicated that the U.S. was rapidly evacuating personnel from embassies and military bases across the Middle East, citing intelligence about potential attacks by Iran on Americans. Additionally, comments from the President at a Florida rally on October 23 hinted that tensions with Iran might escalate again after the midterms.

As stock and bond markets close on weekends, investors often sell cryptocurrency to reduce risk, and Bitcoin is typically the most liquid option. Concerns about rising oil prices—West Texas Intermediate crude reached $107.89 a barrel on October 20, a spike of 13.1% in just a week—fueled inflation worries.

Further compounding the situation, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw a staggering net outflow of $635.5 million on October 22, the largest daily outflow since June, erasing the $528.4 million influx from the day before.

Interest rates don’t seem to be the primary driver of this drop. On October 22, the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.96% from 5.31% earlier in the month, and lower yields usually support Bitcoin. Meanwhile, the VIX, a measure of expected stock market volatility, rose from 14.84 to 19.03, indicating growing apprehension among stock investors.

Leveraged traders could deepen the current downturn. Coinbase ( NASDAQ: COIN | COIN Price Prediction ) noted that the largest cluster of net long Bitcoin positions—trades made with borrowed money that profit from rising prices—averaged at $81,993, with 64% of their dollar value entered at prices above where Bitcoin currently trades.

Liquidation occurs when an exchange must forcibly close a borrowed position because significant losses consume the trader’s collateral. Each liquidation triggers a market sale that can drive further price drops, creating a chain reaction that continues until all over-leveraged positions are cleared. This type of selling often happens quickly and doesn’t necessarily reflect real demand.
Currently, Bitcoin is trading below both its 50-day average of $81,798 and its 20-day average of $82,539, suggesting that many recent buyers are now at a loss, giving short-term sellers an advantage.

Cost basis, or the average price paid by a group of investors, is crucial here. According to Glassnode data, the cost basis for spot ETF holders and treasury companies—public firms holding Bitcoin on their balance sheets—falls between $80,000 and $81,500. A decline below $80,000 could push this group, including ETF buyers who put $6.3 billion into ETFs in Q3 alone, into paper losses.

Glassnode warned in its October 14 report that the largest buy orders on Binance were clustered around $80,000. A close below this ETF cost basis could eliminate the nearest support identified in Bitcoin’s on-chain data. However, the dip occurred on relatively low trading volume compared to the October 24 selloff and quickly reversed, indicating a lack of strong conviction.
Bitcoin has dropped just 3.9%, while Ethereum ( CRYPTO: ETH ) has fallen 12.5% and Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ) has lost 16.1%.

This resilience may stem from Bitcoin’s broader base of long-term buyers, as ETFs and treasury companies hold significant amounts near their cost basis and have an incentive to defend it. In contrast, Ethereum and Solana operate in smaller markets where leveraged trading plays a larger role, and investors tend to sell riskier assets first during periods of uncertainty.

As stock and bond markets close on weekends, investors often sell cryptocurrency to reduce risk, and Bitcoin is typically the most liquid option. Concerns about rising oil prices—West Texas Intermediate crude reached $107.89 a barrel on October 20, a spike of 13.1% in just a week—fueled inflation worries.

Further compounding the situation, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw a staggering net outflow of $635.5 million on October 22, the largest daily outflow since June, erasing the $528.4 million influx from the day before.

Interest rates don’t seem to be the primary driver of this drop. On October 22, the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.96% from 5.31% earlier in the month, and lower yields usually support Bitcoin. Meanwhile, the VIX, a measure of expected stock market volatility, rose from 14.84 to 19.03, indicating growing apprehension among stock investors.

Leveraged traders could deepen the current downturn. Coinbase ( NASDAQ: COIN | COIN Price Prediction ) noted that the largest cluster of net long Bitcoin positions—trades made with borrowed money that profit from rising prices—averaged at $81,993, with 64% of their dollar value entered at prices above where Bitcoin currently trades.

Liquidation occurs when an exchange must forcibly close a borrowed position because significant losses consume the trader’s collateral. Each liquidation triggers a market sale that can drive further price drops, creating a chain reaction that continues until all over-leveraged positions are cleared. This type of selling often happens quickly and doesn’t necessarily reflect real demand.
Currently, Bitcoin is trading below both its 50-day average of $81,798 and its 20-day average of $82,539, suggesting that many recent buyers are now at a loss, giving short-term sellers an advantage.

Cost basis, or the average price paid by a group of investors, is crucial here. According to Glassnode data, the cost basis for spot ETF holders and treasury companies—public firms holding Bitcoin on their balance sheets—falls between $80,000 and $81,500. A decline below $80,000 could push this group, including ETF buyers who put $6.3 billion into ETFs in Q3 alone, into paper losses.

Glassnode warned in its October 14 report that the largest buy orders on Binance were clustered around $80,000. A close below this ETF cost basis could eliminate the nearest support identified in Bitcoin’s on-chain data. However, the dip occurred on relatively low trading volume compared to the October 24 selloff and quickly reversed, indicating a lack of strong conviction.
Bitcoin has dropped just 3.9%, while Ethereum ( CRYPTO: ETH ) has fallen 12.5% and Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ) has lost 16.1%.

This resilience may stem from Bitcoin’s broader base of long-term buyers, as ETFs and treasury companies hold significant amounts near their cost basis and have an incentive to defend it. In contrast, Ethereum and Solana operate in smaller markets where leveraged trading plays a larger role, and investors tend to sell riskier assets first during periods of uncertainty.

If Bitcoin cannot reclaim $81,500, $77,600 appears to be the next significant level to watch. This target aligns with Glassnode’s True Market Mean—the average price paid by active investors, excluding coins that have remained inactive for years—and sits about 3.3% below the current price. passages: Strategy Inc. ( NASDAQ: MSTR ) experienced an $8.3 billion paper loss on its Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) holdings in the second quarter, largely due to a drop in the cryptocurrency's price.
The company is expected to announce its Q3 earnings on October 29, 2026, though it has not yet been officially confirmed.
The big question now is whether Strategy can turn that significant loss into a third-quarter profit.
Strategy's $8.32 billion Q2 Bitcoin loss could reverse in Q3 after Bitcoin surged 42.8%, ending the quarter above the company's $75,446 average acquisition cost.
In its second-quarter report released on July 30, Strategy reported a net loss of $8.22 billion.
Strategy has continued to acquire Bitcoin, as its October 19 filing showed it purchased 267 BTC, valued at around $22.1 million, between October 12 and 18 at an average price of $82,900.
This brings its total Bitcoin holdings to 848,517 BTC, which were purchased at a total cost of $64.02 billion, averaging $75,446 per coin.
The potential unrealized gain from Bitcoin will be a key focus.
By the end of Q2, the market value of their Bitcoin holdings was $49.7 billion, compared to a $63.9 billion cost basis.

Analysts' EPS estimates for Q3 vary widely, ranging from -$0.99 to $52.82, reflecting different assumptions about Bitcoin's quarter-end price.
If Bitcoin remains below its September 30 close of $83,556 through December 31, Strategy could lose some of its Q3 gains in its next quarterly report.

Strategy Inc. ( NASDAQ: MSTR | MSTR Price Prediction ) experienced an $8.3 billion paper loss on its Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ) holdings in the second quarter, largely due to a drop in the cryptocurrency’s price. The company is expected to announce its Q3 earnings on October 29, 2026, though it has not yet been officially confirmed. The big question now is whether Strategy can turn that significant loss into a third-quarter profit.

In its second-quarter report released on July 30, Strategy reported a net loss of $8.22 billion. A whopping $8.32 billion in unrealized Bitcoin losses drove that result, reflecting a decline in value that hit overall earnings. The company’s earnings per share (EPS) fell to -$24.45, missing expectations of $3.07, while revenue was $122.4 million.

These losses stem from fair value accounting, which requires companies to adjust asset values to reflect current market prices at the end of each quarter. Bitcoin closed on June 30 at $58,524 but climbed to $83,556 by September 30, marking a 42.8% increase during the quarter.

Strategy has continued to acquire Bitcoin , as its October 19 filing showed it purchased 267 BTC, valued at around $22.1 million, between October 12 and 18 at an average price of $82,900. This brings its total Bitcoin holdings to 848,517 BTC , which were purchased at a total cost of $64.02 billion, averaging $75,446 per coin.
As of October 23, MSTR shares were priced at $146, down 10% over the month but up 6.7% over the past week.
Analysts are hopeful for a return to profitability in Q3, with consensus estimates projecting earnings of $17.98 per share, compared to $8.42 during the same period last year.
Analysts’ EPS estimates for Q3 vary widely, ranging from -$0.99 to $52.82, reflecting different assumptions about Bitcoin’s quarter-end price.

The potential unrealized gain from Bitcoin will be a key focus. With Bitcoin closing at $83,556 on September 30, prices were above Strategy’s average acquisition cost of $75,446, suggesting the company may report Q3 gains. By the end of Q2, the market value of their Bitcoin holdings was $49.7 billion, compared to a $63.9 billion cost basis.

Another key topic is the company’s preferred stock, STRC. This type of stock takes priority over common shares for dividends. The recent filing reported $193.1 million in STRC buybacks and an increased buyback authorization of $3 billion, with $1.16 billion remaining. In July, CEO Phong Le noted that buying STRC shares below par would reduce future dividend obligations.

Shareholders will also vote on October 28 on paying STRC dividends daily rather than twice a month, at the current annual rate of 12%. If approved, these daily dividends could start on November 1, allowing stockholders to earn dividends for each day they own shares without worrying about specific record dates. This change could help stabilize the price fluctuations that STRC typically experiences around ex-dividend dates.

Michael Saylor stirred interest on October 23 with a post stating, “Just resolving a few Bitcoin matters behind closed doors.” Investors will likely seek clarification on this comment, as well as updates on other revenue streams, such as subscription revenue, which rose 54% in Q2 to $62.9 million. Additionally, concerns are growing regarding Strategy’s potential removal from MSCI indexes .

Yes, Strategy could report a substantial unrealized gain for Q3, given Bitcoin’s rising value, which ended the quarter 42.8% higher than where it started. However, Bitcoin’s price has dipped since September 30, trading just above $80,000, marking a 3.9% decline over the past month.

This recent decrease affects only Q4, as Q3 ended on September 30. If Bitcoin remains below its September 30 close of $83,556 through December 31, Strategy could lose some of its Q3 gains in its next quarterly report.

The company is expected to announce its Q3 earnings on October 29, 2026, though it has not yet been officially confirmed. The big question now is whether Strategy can turn that significant loss into a third-quarter profit.

In its second-quarter report released on July 30, Strategy reported a net loss of $8.22 billion. A whopping $8.32 billion in unrealized Bitcoin losses drove that result, reflecting a decline in value that hit overall earnings. The company’s earnings per share (EPS) fell to -$24.45, missing expectations of $3.07, while revenue was $122.4 million.

These losses stem from fair value accounting, which requires companies to adjust asset values to reflect current market prices at the end of each quarter. Bitcoin closed on June 30 at $58,524 but climbed to $83,556 by September 30, marking a 42.8% increase during the quarter.

Strategy has continued to acquire Bitcoin , as its October 19 filing showed it purchased 267 BTC, valued at around $22.1 million, between October 12 and 18 at an average price of $82,900. This brings its total Bitcoin holdings to 848,517 BTC , which were purchased at a total cost of $64.02 billion, averaging $75,446 per coin.
As of October 23, MSTR shares were priced at $146, down 10% over the month but up 6.7% over the past week.
Analysts are hopeful for a return to profitability in Q3, with consensus estimates projecting earnings of $17.98 per share, compared to $8.42 during the same period last year.
Analysts’ EPS estimates for Q3 vary widely, ranging from -$0.99 to $52.82, reflecting different assumptions about Bitcoin’s quarter-end price.

The potential unrealized gain from Bitcoin will be a key focus. With Bitcoin closing at $83,556 on September 30, prices were above Strategy’s average acquisition cost of $75,446, suggesting the company may report Q3 gains. By the end of Q2, the market value of their Bitcoin holdings was $49.7 billion, compared to a $63.9 billion cost basis.

Another key topic is the company’s preferred stock, STRC. This type of stock takes priority over common shares for dividends. The recent filing reported $193.1 million in STRC buybacks and an increased buyback authorization of $3 billion, with $1.16 billion remaining. In July, CEO Phong Le noted that buying STRC shares below par would reduce future dividend obligations.

Shareholders will also vote on October 28 on paying STRC dividends daily rather than twice a month, at the current annual rate of 12%. If approved, these daily dividends could start on November 1, allowing stockholders to earn dividends for each day they own shares without worrying about specific record dates. This change could help stabilize the price fluctuations that STRC typically experiences around ex-dividend dates.

Michael Saylor stirred interest on October 23 with a post stating, “Just resolving a few Bitcoin matters behind closed doors.” Investors will likely seek clarification on this comment, as well as updates on other revenue streams, such as subscription revenue, which rose 54% in Q2 to $62.9 million. Additionally, concerns are growing regarding Strategy’s potential removal from MSCI indexes .

Yes, Strategy could report a substantial unrealized gain for Q3, given Bitcoin’s rising value, which ended the quarter 42.8% higher than where it started. However, Bitcoin’s price has dipped since September 30, trading just above $80,000, marking a 3.9% decline over the past month.

This recent decrease affects only Q4, as Q3 ended on September 30. If Bitcoin remains below its September 30 close of $83,556 through December 31, Strategy could lose some of its Q3 gains in its next quarterly report.

Correlation measures how closely two assets move together based on their daily returns—the percentage change from one day's closing price to the next. A correlation of 1 means the two assets rise and fall together, while a value near zero indicates no significant relationship. Correlation primarily tracks directional movements rather than the magnitude of price changes. So, if XRP fell only half as much as Bitcoin on certain days, it could still show a high correlation because both assets move together. Traders monitor these correlations as a falling number can signal that two assets are starting to diverge. Unfortunately for XRP, the data shows it moved closer to Bitcoin in the week ending. Its relative stability was more about not falling as much during the same downtrend than about establishing any clear independence. While XRP's minimal weekly change seems promising, its performance over the last month tells a different story. Over the past year, XRP has lost 49.8%, while Bitcoin has decreased by 27.7%. This pattern suggests XRP tends to follow Bitcoin, but often more sharply, suffering more during price drops. A flat performance after a month of steep losses could suggest easing selling pressure. However, it could also signal declining trading activity. For example, spot XRP ETFs traded only $18.8 million on October 23, down from over $102 million on October 2. The only sign of a potential break came in the 24 hours leading up to October 25, when XRP rose 1.4% while Bitcoin fell 0.4%. One key factor that could push XRP away from Bitcoin is the flow of funds into spot XRP ETFs, which directly hold XRP. By comparison, Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ) fell 2%, Ethereum ( CRYPTO: ETH ) fell 3.4%, and Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ) fell 2.8%. With XRP at $1.30 and Bitcoin near $80,268, some XRP holders speculate the token may be starting to decouple from Bitcoin.

Despite its flat performance over the week, the XRP-Bitcoin correlation suggests otherwise. In fact, XRP’s daily returns over the past seven days showed a strong correlation of 0.97 with Bitcoin’s movements, indicating they moved almost identically during this period. Over longer periods, the correlation remains strong: 0.91 over 30 days, 0.89 over 90 days, and 0.85 historically.

This suggests that while XRP appeared stable over the week, it has closely followed Bitcoin’s trends rather than showing separation. Is the perceived independence real, or is XRP simply falling less than Bitcoin?

Correlation measures how closely two assets move together based on their daily returns—the percentage change from one day’s closing price to the next. A correlation of 1 means the two assets rise and fall together, while a value near zero indicates no significant relationship.

Correlation primarily tracks directional movements rather than the magnitude of price changes. So, if XRP fell only half as much as Bitcoin on certain days, it could still show a high correlation because both assets move together.

Traders monitor these correlations as a falling number can signal that two assets are starting to diverge. Unfortunately for XRP, the data shows it moved closer to Bitcoin in the week ending. Its relative stability was more about not falling as much during the same downtrend than about establishing any clear independence.

While XRP’s minimal weekly change seems promising, its performance over the last month tells a different story. Over the past 30 days, XRP has dropped 18.8%, compared with Bitcoin’s relatively mild 5% decline. Year-to-date, XRP is down 29.1%, while Bitcoin is down just 7.7%.
Over the past year, XRP has lost 49.8%, while Bitcoin has decreased by 27.7%. This pattern suggests XRP tends to follow Bitcoin, but often more sharply, suffering more during price drops.

A flat performance after a month of steep losses could suggest easing selling pressure. However, it could also signal declining trading activity. For example, spot XRP ETFs traded only $18.8 million on October 23, down from over $102 million on October 2.

The only sign of a potential break came in the 24 hours leading up to October 25, when XRP rose 1.4% while Bitcoin fell 0.4%. Yet, such a single-day movement does little to affect the broader 30-day correlation.

One key factor that could push XRP away from Bitcoin is the flow of funds into spot XRP ETFs, which directly hold XRP. From October 19 to October 23, these funds saw a net inflow of about $4.3 million, including significant inflows of around $709,000 on October 21 and $3.5 million on October 22.

However, these ETFs’ net assets shrank from $1.77 billion on September 25 to $1.48 billion on October 23, indicating that price declines outweighed the inflows. A few million dollars per day is clearly insufficient to steer XRP away from Bitcoin’s influence.

Additionally, the upcoming Ripple Swell conference from October 27 to 29 in New York, combined with XRPL Apex, Ripple’s developer conference, could matter. While past conferences haven’t led to long-lasting rallies for XRP, any agreements related to payments or tokenized assets on the XRP Ledger could generate demand independent of Bitcoin.

Short selling also presents another possibility. Reports indicated a rise in XRP margin shorts on Bitfinex, increasing from approximately 148,850 to around 300,000 in under two weeks. While these figures are unconfirmed, if XRP begins to rise, short sellers may be forced to buy back coins, creating a short squeeze that drives up demand for XRP.

In conclusion, XRP has not broken away from Bitcoin. During the week ending October 25, it fell less than Bitcoin while still closely tracking its movements, resulting in a correlation of 0.97. This relationship shows that XRP continues to follow Bitcoin’s lead rather than forge its own path. One week is too short to suggest separation, especially given a month in which XRP plummeted 18.8% while Bitcoin lost only 5%.

However, two potential shifts could change this narrative. First, spot XRP ETFs need consistent daily inflows near the $22.6 million they saw on September 25, rather than days with no inflow, as seen in October. Additionally, XRP must close above its 50-day average around $1.41 on days when Bitcoin declines, as this would strengthen its potential to break free from Bitcoin’s grasp.

extraction.body: Your Mac comes with a fairly robust suite of built-in privacy tools. If you think about it too hard, you'll start sweating at the reality of how much personal data you have on your MacBook . Whether it's sensitive documents or credentials and logins, you'd probably like to keep all of it secure. And while Apple has built its brand around being particularly privacy- and security-focused, that doesn't mean you shouldn't take the time to go through your settings and make sure your MacBook is as safe as it can be. After all, something like hopping on an unsecured public Wi-Fi network could leave you vulnerable, and not everyone has the best habits when it comes to protections like passwords. Your individual privacy and security needs will vary depending on who you are, what you do and how you do it. While this list isn't exhaustive, it's a place to start. So, if it's been a while, or perhaps you've just bought a new MacBook, it might be time to take a spin through your privacy settings. From location services to your lock screen password, here are some areas you should double-check. One of the first ways you can make your MacBook more secure is by using a strong passcode and setting up Touch ID. Your pet's name or your birthday isn't going to cut it. This is especially important if you don't always have eyes on your MacBook. You can require a password to wake your laptop up from sleep or your screensaver. You also have the option to decide how long your laptop must be asleep before prompting. To tweak these settings, go to System Settings > Lock Screen . Another setting to revisit is Location Services. Location Services is what lets apps, websites or the like get information about where you are. In cases like Google or Apple Maps, it can be useful and even necessary for the app to work. It's worth considering, though, that not every app that's accessing your location needs to. If you go to Settings, then Privacy & Security, you'll find Location Services. There you can either wholesale turn everything off, or individually grant or revoke apps' access to your location. Similarly, you can decide which apps have access to your camera and microphone by checking those individual settings under Privacy & Security and toggling your choices on or off. Odds are, when you're on your MacBook, you're likely also on a Wi-Fi network . You can actually decide how your MacBook joins those Wi-Fi networks. If you go to Settings > Wi-Fi, make sure your computer doesn't automatically join unsecured Wi-Fi networks, which could open you up to malware or data interception . One of the settings options will send you a notification asking for permission before joining anything. That way, you can stay in control. On the topic of exercising control, your MacBook comes with a Firewall option that's off by default. Firewall stops any connections from other networks or the internet that you don't want, particularly if you're on public Wi-Fi. To turn it on, you can go to System Settings > Network > Firewall. In an age of algorithms, you're probably used to seeing personalized ads . Apple, among others, collects data on you that it uses to serve you ads in spots like the App Store or Apple News. There are a few steps you can take to modify or put a stop to this. If you go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Apple Advertising > View Ad Targeting Information , you can see what Apple knows about you. The company notes that it doesn't track you across websites or third-party apps. You can also just toggle off Personalized Ads. A note on the settings page says this limits "Apple's ability to deliver relevant ads," but it does not impact how many ads you see. In terms of controlling the amount of information you give Apple, you can also change the settings around Analytics & Improvements. According to Apple, this anonymous analytics information helps its developers improve its products, as it can include info on events like system crashes and freezes or general usage. The data also includes hardware and software specifications, what operating system you're on, as well as which apps you're using, to name a few. With permission, Apple might also share info like crash data with third-party developers. Your analytics data then gets deleted after a month. An article from Consumer Reports found some experts were split on exactly how risky sharing analytics data is, noting it often depends on the companies involved. If you'd just rather not take the risk , you can go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics Improvements and toggle off several choices like Improve Siri & Dictation and Share with App Developers. In any case, a periodic check-in with your settings can help keep your private info secure as you and your MacBook venture out into the world.

passages: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has put the annual cost of licensing the company’s AI software at around $2,000 per GPU to 'run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,' according to a recent video of the comments (below), a pricing model that could generate $50 billion over five years under a proposed scenario involving five million paid licenses outlined by FourWeekMBA .
It’s also unclear which software the license would cover, or if there is overlap between products.
The distinction matters because Nvidia already charges for enterprise software.
Its AI Enterprise platform is listed at $4,500 per GPU for a one-year subscription.
It should not be treated as a confirmed price cut.
Enterprises deploying AI agents need security, governance and someone accountable for keeping the stack running.
My bet: OpenShell becomes the standard security layer for enterprise AI, driving adoption of NVIDIA’s paid software and support.
Each new year of GPU sales adds another potential stream of software revenue.
Nvidia had previously introduced its Open Agent Safety Platform in September.
The newer reference architecture builds on that effort, extending the approach to enterprise infrastructure and edge systems.
Tom's Hardware is part of Future US Inc, an international media group and leading digital publisher.
The licensing discussion comes as Nvidia develops more of the infrastructure needed to deploy and manage AI agents in enterprise environments.
These systems can use tools, access data, and execute tasks, creating new security and management challenges for businesses running them at scale.

On October 21, Nvidia announced its OpenShell Reference Architecture , a system that combines its Vera Rubin computing infrastructure, Vera CPUs, and BlueField-4 data processing units (DPUs) running Nvidia Sentry.
OpenShell provides a secure runtime for AI agents , establishing boundaries around their actions and access to tools and resources.
Sentry monitors agent activity independently and can quarantine an agent that attempts to cross those boundaries, according to Nvidia.
The architecture is designed to bring security controls into the underlying infrastructure rather than relying solely on safeguards built into an AI model or application.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has put the annual cost of licensing the company’s AI software at around $2,000 per GPU to 'run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,' according to a recent video of the comments (below), a pricing model that could generate $50 billion over five years under a proposed scenario involving five million paid licenses outlined by FourWeekMBA . Huang discussed the pricing at GTC Berlin on October 22, where the company outlined its broader push to build an AI infrastructure business spanning chips, software and AI-agent security . “Software licensing will become increasingly a major part of our company’s business. The way that we license will be…for example, it’s about $2,000 per GPU per year to run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,” said Huang. The numbers add up quickly. At $2,000 per GPU each year, Nvidia would bring in $10 billion annually if five million GPUs were covered by paid licenses. Over five years, that would amount to $50 billion, provided customers kept renewing their subscriptions. The catch, however, is that Nvidia has not disclosed how many GPUs could be covered by the proposed $2,000 fee, or whether that’s its standard price. It’s also unclear which software the license would cover, or if there is overlap between products. The distinction matters because Nvidia already charges for enterprise software. Its AI Enterprise platform is listed at $4,500 per GPU for a one-year subscription. Huang’s reported $2,000 figure is lower, but Nvidia has not confirmed that the two prices cover the same products or licensing terms. It should not be treated as a confirmed price cut. Jensen’s ~$2,000 per GPU per year in enterprise software deserves more attention. Enterprises deploying AI agents need security, governance and someone accountable for keeping the stack running. My bet: OpenShell becomes the standard security layer for enterprise AI, driving adoption of NVIDIA’s paid software and support. Consider the math. Assume: • 10M eligible enterprise GPUs shipped in a year • 50% paid software attach • $2,000 per GPU annually That’s $10B in annual recurring revenue potential. Keep those subscriptions for five years and you get $50B from a single year’s GPU shipments. Each new year of GPU sales adds another potential stream of software revenue. $NVDA October 22, 2026 The licensing discussion comes as Nvidia develops more of the infrastructure needed to deploy and manage AI agents in enterprise environments. These systems can use tools, access data, and execute tasks, creating new security and management challenges for businesses running them at scale. On October 21, Nvidia announced its OpenShell Reference Architecture , a system that combines its Vera Rubin computing infrastructure, Vera CPUs, and BlueField-4 data processing units (DPUs) running Nvidia Sentry. OpenShell provides a secure runtime for AI agents , establishing boundaries around their actions and access to tools and resources. Sentry monitors agent activity independently and can quarantine an agent that attempts to cross those boundaries, according to Nvidia. The architecture is designed to bring security controls into the underlying infrastructure rather than relying solely on safeguards built into an AI model or application. Nvidia had previously introduced its Open Agent Safety Platform in September. The newer reference architecture builds on that effort, extending the approach to enterprise infrastructure and edge systems. Anthropic is integrating OpenShell and BlueField hardware with Claude Managed Agents to give businesses additional control over what their AI agents can access inside execution sandboxes. Salesforce has developed a Slack Admin Bridge for OpenShell that lets administrators review agent access requests, approve or reject permissions, and monitor activity directly in Slack. The proposed software pricing fits Huang’s wider argument that Nvidia is becoming more than a supplier of GPUs. The company has expanded into networking, systems, enterprise software, and infrastructure designed to run AI workloads. Speaking on the BG2Pod podcast recently, Huang said, “One of these days, people might not categorize us as a chip company anymore.” He pointed to Nvidia’s presence across industries including healthcare, automotive, telecommunications and life sciences, where the company provides broader technology stacks rather than chips alone. That said, Nvidia has not said when the $2,000-per-GPU fee would take effect or which software it would cover. It also remains unclear how the proposed pricing would fit into the company’s existing enterprise software business. Nvidia’s reported $2,000 annual fee per GPU could turn its software business into a multibillion-dollar revenue stream, but Huang has yet to reveal when the pricing could take effect.
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has put the annual cost of licensing the company’s AI software at around $2,000 per GPU to 'run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,' according to a recent video of the comments (below), a pricing model that could generate $50 billion over five years under a proposed scenario involving five million paid licenses outlined by FourWeekMBA .

Huang discussed the pricing at GTC Berlin on October 22, where the company outlined its broader push to build an AI infrastructure business spanning chips, software and AI-agent security . “Software licensing will become increasingly a major part of our company’s business. The way that we license will be…for example, it’s about $2,000 per GPU per year to run all the software that Nvidia provides that runs agents on these AI factories,” said Huang.

The numbers add up quickly. At $2,000 per GPU each year, Nvidia would bring in $10 billion annually if five million GPUs were covered by paid licenses. Over five years, that would amount to $50 billion, provided customers kept renewing their subscriptions. The catch, however, is that Nvidia has not disclosed how many GPUs could be covered by the proposed $2,000 fee, or whether that’s its standard price. It’s also unclear which software the license would cover, or if there is overlap between products.

The distinction matters because Nvidia already charges for enterprise software. Its AI Enterprise platform is listed at $4,500 per GPU for a one-year subscription. Huang’s reported $2,000 figure is lower, but Nvidia has not confirmed that the two prices cover the same products or licensing terms. It should not be treated as a confirmed price cut.

Jensen’s ~$2,000 per GPU per year in enterprise software deserves more attention. Enterprises deploying AI agents need security, governance and someone accountable for keeping the stack running. My bet: OpenShell becomes the standard security layer for enterprise AI, driving adoption of NVIDIA’s paid software and support. Consider the math. Assume: • 10M eligible enterprise GPUs shipped in a year • 50% paid software attach • $2,000 per GPU annually That’s $10B in annual recurring revenue potential. Keep those subscriptions for five years and you get $50B from a single year’s GPU shipments. Each new year of GPU sales adds another potential stream of software revenue. $NVDA October 22, 2026

The licensing discussion comes as Nvidia develops more of the infrastructure needed to deploy and manage AI agents in enterprise environments. These systems can use tools, access data, and execute tasks, creating new security and management challenges for businesses running them at scale.

On October 21, Nvidia announced its OpenShell Reference Architecture , a system that combines its Vera Rubin computing infrastructure, Vera CPUs, and BlueField-4 data processing units (DPUs) running Nvidia Sentry. OpenShell provides a secure runtime for AI agents , establishing boundaries around their actions and access to tools and resources. Sentry monitors agent activity independently and can quarantine an agent that attempts to cross those boundaries, according to Nvidia. The architecture is designed to bring security controls into the underlying infrastructure rather than relying solely on safeguards built into an AI model or application.

Nvidia had previously introduced its Open Agent Safety Platform in September. The newer reference architecture builds on that effort, extending the approach to enterprise infrastructure and edge systems.

Other companies are also incorporating these controls into their products. Anthropic is integrating OpenShell and BlueField hardware with Claude Managed Agents to give businesses additional control over what their AI agents can access inside execution sandboxes. Salesforce has developed a Slack Admin Bridge for OpenShell that lets administrators review agent access requests, approve or reject permissions, and monitor activity directly in Slack.

The proposed software pricing fits Huang’s wider argument that Nvidia is becoming more than a supplier of GPUs. The company has expanded into networking, systems, enterprise software, and infrastructure designed to run AI workloads. Speaking on the BG2Pod podcast recently, Huang said, “One of these days, people might not categorize us as a chip company anymore.” He pointed to Nvidia’s presence across industries including healthcare, automotive, telecommunications and life sciences, where the company provides broader technology stacks rather than chips alone.

That said, Nvidia has not said when the $2,000-per-GPU fee would take effect or which software it would cover. It also remains unclear how the proposed pricing would fit into the company’s existing enterprise software business.
